newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Speculative demand for dollars out of London coupled with local importer buying drew the Reserve Bank in to the currency market in defence of the rand as it moved above the 4.70 level, dealers said.
After moving to an intraday high of 4.7055 bid against the dollar, the rand retraced to 4.6975/7025 by the local close from 4.6985/7035 overnight. Volumes on the day were generally thin.

Dealers said the currency was under fire from the start from London-based players looking to take a punt. Small-scale importer demand contributed to the rand's weakness and it breached its day's weakest level by 0730 GMT.
"It's been a quiet day with offshore guys buying dollars and the importers buying a bit also," a dealer said," and the SARB (Reserve Bank) supplied the market with a few dollars."
Bertus van Zyl, general manager of the Reserve Bank's international banking division, confirmed the central bank had offered dollars to the market but on a very small scale.
"Yes we have been in the market but in very small amounts," he said.
Dealers said that despite the intervention, the rand was expected to continue weakening in the week ahead.

"What we have seen in the last couple of weeks is importers and offshore guys looking to buy dollars and that should continue next week. The rand has more potential to weaken further next week than to strengthen," a dealer said.
She added that she expected the currency to weaken to between 4.73 and 4.75 against the dollar next week.
The bond market shrugged off the currency's weakness, focussing instead on a sharp improvement in the country's money supply and credit extension.

Reserve Bank statistics released on Thursday showed credit extension to the private sector -- cited by central bank Governor Chris Stals as one of his main bugbears when he hiked interest rates last November -- grew at a rate of 17.1 percent year-on-year in November from 18.86 percent in October.
Economists polled by Reuters had expected credit extension growth to slow to 18.2 with the lowest forecast at 17.5.
Money supply growth also beat expectations, rising 15.32 percent against economists' forecasts of 15.5 percent.
"We came down to a low of 16.125 (percent) on the back of the data," a dealer said. "There was good institutional buying in the 16.20s and short-covering brought it down to around 16.12," he added.
Dealers said the market could strengthen further next week as more institutional players returned from their Christmas holidays.
Signs of an easing of pressure on the money market would also boost sentiment, a dealer said.
The money market shortage eased to 9.127 billion rand on Thursday from 10.448 billion rand on Tuesday.
Money market rates were unchanged, however, with three-month NCD rates steady at between 17.40 and 17.75 percent while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at 16.70 to 17.00 percent.
Bond Exchange statistics showed foreigners sold a net 97.16 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Thursday after selling 43.85 million rand on Tuesday.
Nominal cumulative turnover was 1.64 billion rand on Thursday from 562.4 million rand on Tuesday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
